These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Round monetary Decimal results only via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Signal domain failures by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a stable snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, and put the offending value in the detail via `repr`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)

texts.at-0001: Round money only with round_money Round monetary Decimal results only via ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
texts.at-0002: Normalize money inputs with to_money Always pass monetary values through `to_money` from `ledgerly.money` before storing or comparing them; it rejects floats with a `float_amount` BillingError and returns a Decimal. Compare against `ZERO` from the same module rather than a literal.
texts.at-0003: Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes Signal domain failures by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with a stable snake_case code such as `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity` or `negative_amount`, and put the offending value in the detail via `repr`.
texts.at-0004: Guard mutations on invoice draft status Mutating invoice operations must first check `invoice.status != "draft"` and raise `BillingError("invalid_state", ...)`, matching the existing guard in `issue_invoice`.

item.title: Normalize datetimes with ensure_utc
item.content: In ledgerly, normalize every incoming datetime with `ensure_utc` from `ledgerly.clock` before comparing or doing arithmetic (see `current_period` in `ledgerly/subscriptions.py`).
